suites.scope: Actual SQLite HTTP server and shared web UI. Empty map-style fixture isolates UI races; does not validate real map tiles or native devices.
checks: Shared UI starts, renders bounded quests and initializes map without AbortSignal static methods
Late next-page response cannot append the previous query into newer quest search
Late polling response cannot overwrite search performed while polling was in flight
Failed location cleanup still revokes the session and failed subsequent refresh leaves no private UI

suites.scope: Actual SQLite API with admin MFA, 237 synthetic billing orders and mobile web UI. Minimal map-style fixture.
checks: Admin reaches all 237 billing orders through bounded pages, including oldest pending payment
Delayed privileged billing page cannot replace a later profile screen
Reopening billing resets pagination and payment controls fit a 320px viewport

suites.scope: Real service-worker lifecycle using archived v0.6 worker and current v0.7 worker. Minimal version-labelled HTTP shell fixture, not a full native-device test.
checks: Archived v0.6 worker installs and controls its original shell
Existing v0.6 installation upgrades on closing all controlled tabs and reopening
Active v0.7 worker keeps HTML and modules from its own release while newer worker waits
Next launch activates new shell atomically and removes obsolete shell caches

limitations: These are 11 new v0.7 scenarios; historical v0.6 checks were not counted as current passes.
Map resources use an empty style fixture to isolate UI races; no current real-tile availability claim.
Service-worker lifecycle uses real archived v0.6 and current v0.7 workers with a minimal version-labelled HTTP shell.

A previously installed v0.6 worker still has its original network-first HTML behavior until activation of v0.7. Close all controlled tabs/windows and relaunch to upgrade. The stronger same-release reload guarantee applies after v0.7 activation.
Native-device testing, external IdP and Android/iOS signing remain separate release gates.
